Let \(N\ge 1\), \(m\ge 2\), and assume the following: \(1<p<\frac{2^*}{2}\) if \(N\ge 3\), and \(p>1\) if \(N=1,2\), where \(2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}\) for \(N\ge 3\); \(\mu_i>0\) for \(i=1,\dots,m\); \(\lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{ji}<0\) for all \(i\ne j\); and \(Q_\varepsilon(x-y_i):=Q(\varepsilon x-y_i)\), where \(Q\in C(\mathbb{R}^N)\) is nonnegative, has bounded support, and there exist exactly pairwise distinct points \(y_1,\dots,y_m\in\mathbb{R}^N\) such that \(Q(-y_i)=\|Q\|_\infty\) for all \(i=1,\dots,m\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), consider the coupled elliptic system
\[
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u_i + u_i
= \mu_i Q_\varepsilon(x-y_i) |u_i|^{2p-2}u_i
+ \displaystyle\sum_{j\neq i} \lambda_{ij} |u_j|^{p} |u_i|^{p-2}u_i, \\[4pt]
u_i \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),\quad i=1,\dots,m,
\end{cases}
\]
and write \(\mathbf u=(u_1,\dots,u_m)\in H\) with \(H=(H^1(\mathbb R^N))^m\). Let \(J_\varepsilon\) denote the associated energy functional. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of sign-changing solutions for this system under these assumptions?

Options:
A. There exists \(\varepsilon_0>0\) such that for every \(0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0\), the system admits a sequence of sign-changing solutions \(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\in H\) with
\[
0<J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(1)}_\varepsilon\bigr)<\cdots<J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\bigr)<J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k+1)}_\varepsilon\bigr)<\cdots,
\]
and
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\bigr)=+\infty,
\]
but this multiplicity conclusion is available only for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), not for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).
B. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the system admits a least-energy sign-changing solution \(\mathbf u_\varepsilon\in H\), and up to the natural sign symmetry \(\mathbf u\mapsto-\mathbf u\), this is the only sign-changing solution guaranteed by the theory.
C. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the system admits infinitely many distinct sign-changing solutions \(\mathbf u\in H\).
D. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the system admits infinitely many sign-changing solutions \(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\in H\), but their energy levels remain bounded above for that fixed \(\varepsilon\); equivalently, there exists \(C_\varepsilon<\infty\) such that
\[
J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\bigr)\le C_\varepsilon\qquad\text{for all }k.
\]
E. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the system admits a sequence of sign-changing solutions \(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon=(u^{(k)}_{\varepsilon,1},\dots,u^{(k)}_{\varepsilon,m})\in H\), indexed by positive integers \(k\), such that
\[
0<J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(1)}_\varepsilon\bigr)
<\cdots< J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\bigr)
< J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k+1)}_\varepsilon\bigr)
<\cdots,
\]
and
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty} J_\varepsilon\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(k)}_\varepsilon\bigr)=+\infty.
\]

Let \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{C}^4\) be the unknown spinor field in the nonlinear Dirac-type equation
\[
-i\gamma^0\gamma^k\partial_k\psi + m\gamma^0\psi - a\psi - \nabla F(\psi)=0,
\]
where \(k=1,2,3\) is summed over, \(\gamma^0,\gamma^k\) are the Dirac matrices, \(m\) and \(a\) are given parameters, and \(F:\mathbb{C}^4\to\mathbb{R}\) is a nonlinearity satisfying the assumptions \((F1)\)–\((F5)\). Here, “periodic” means spatially periodic in \(x\in\mathbb{R}^3\), and “nontrivial” means that \(\psi\not\equiv 0\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of periodic \(C^1\) solutions of this equation under these assumptions?

Options:
A. There exists a unique periodic solution \(\psi\) of
\[
-i\gamma^0\gamma^k\partial_k\psi + m\gamma^0\psi - a\psi - \nabla F(\psi)=0
\]
and this solution belongs to \(C^1\).
B. There exists at least one periodic solution \(\psi\) of
\[
-i\gamma^0\gamma^k\partial_k\psi + m\gamma^0\psi - a\psi - \nabla F(\psi)=0
\]
that belongs to \(C^1\).
C. For every prescribed triple of positive spatial periods \((T_1,T_2,T_3)\), there exists at least one nontrivial solution \(\psi\in C^1\) of
\[
-i\gamma^0\gamma^k\partial_k\psi + m\gamma^0\psi - a\psi - \nabla F(\psi)=0
\]
that is periodic with periods \(T_1,T_2,T_3\) in the three coordinate directions.
D. There exists at least one nontrivial periodic solution \(\psi\) of
\[
-i\gamma^0\gamma^k\partial_k\psi + m\gamma^0\psi - a\psi - \nabla F(\psi)=0
\]
that belongs to \(C^1\), and every periodic \(C^1\) solution of this equation is nontrivial.
E. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

Let \(N=2\) or \(N=3\). Assume \(\gamma\in[1,\infty)\) when \(N=2\), and \(\gamma\in[1,8/3)\) when \(N=3\). Let \(\bar\rho>0\), and let the initial data \((\rho_0,u_0)\) satisfy \(0<\underline\varrho\le \rho_0\le \bar\varrho\) for some positive constants \(\underline\varrho,\bar\varrho\), with \(\rho_0-\bar\rho\in H^3(\mathbb R^N)\) and \(u_0\in H^2(\mathbb R^N)\). Consider the Cauchy problem on \(\mathbb R^N\)
\[
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho u)=0,
\qquad
\partial_t(\rho u)+\nabla\cdot(\rho u\otimes u)+\nabla P(\rho)=\nabla\cdot\bigl(2\rho\mathcal D(u)\bigr)+\nabla\cdot\bigl(\rho\nabla\nabla\log\rho\bigr),
\]
with pressure law \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\) and far-field behavior \(\rho(x,t)\to\bar\rho>0\) and \(u(x,t)\to0\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), where \(\mathcal D(u)=(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)/2\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for this problem?

Options:
A. There exists a unique global strong solution \((\rho,u)\) such that for every \(T>0\) there is a constant \(C(T)>0\), depending on \(T\) and the initial data, with \((C(T))^{-1}\le \rho(x,t)\le C(T)\) for all \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^N\times[0,T]\), and
\[
\rho-\bar\rho\in C([0,T];H^3(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^4(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[
\rho_t\in C([0,T];H^1(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[
u\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)),
\qquad
u_t\in L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1(\mathbb R^N)).
\]
B. There exists a unique global strong solution \((\rho,u)\) such that there is a constant \(C>0\), depending on the initial data but not on \(T\), with \(C^{-1}\le \rho(x,t)\le C\) for all \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^N\times[0,\infty)\), and for every \(T>0\),
\[
\rho-\bar\rho\in C([0,T];H^3(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^4(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[
\rho_t\in C([0,T];H^1(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[\nu\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)),
\qquad
\nu_t\in L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1(\mathbb R^N)).
\]
C. There exists a unique global strong solution \((\rho,u)\) such that for every \(T>0\) there is a constant \(C(T)>0\), depending on \(T\) and the initial data, with \((C(T))^{-1}\le \rho(x,t)\le C(T)\) for all \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^N\times[0,T]\), and
\[
\rho-\bar\rho\in C([0,T];H^3(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^4(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[
\rho_t\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[\nu\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)),
\qquad
\nu_t\in L^\infty(0,T;H^1(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\mathbb R^N)).
\]
D. There exists a unique global strong solution \((\rho,u)\) such that for every \(T>0\) there is a constant \(C(T)>0\), depending on \(T\) and the initial data, and there is a constant \(c_0>0\), depending only on the initial data, with \(c_0\le \rho(x,t)\le C(T)\) for all \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^N\times[0,T]\), and
\[
\rho-\bar\rho\in C([0,T];H^3(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^4(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[
\rho_t\in C([0,T];H^1(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\mathbb R^N)),
\]
\[\nu\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)),
\qquad
\nu_t\in L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1(\mathbb R^N)).
\]
E. There exists a global strong solution \((\rho,u)\) such that for every \(T>0\) there is a constant \(C(T)>0\), depending on \(T\) and the initial data, with \((C(T))^{-1}\le \rho(x,t)\le C(T)\) for all \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^N\times[0,T]\), and
\[
\rho-\bar\rho\in C([0,T];H^3(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^4(\mathbb R^N)),
\qquad
\nu\in C([0,T];H^2(\mathbb R^N))\cap L^2(0,T;H^3(\mathbb R^N)).
\]

Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain containing a field of characteristic $0$, and let $X\subset \mathbb{P}^n_A$ be a closed subscheme that is smooth over $\operatorname{Spec} A$. If $\mathcal I\subset \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}$ is the ideal sheaf of $X$, write $X_t$ for the $t$-th thickening of $X$, i.e. the closed subscheme defined by $\mathcal I^t$ for $t\ge 1$. Fix an integer $j$ and set $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}(j)$. For a nonzero element $a\in A$, let $A_a$ denote the localization of $A$ at the powers of $a$. Which of the following is the strongest consequence of the assumptions above?

Options:
A. There exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ such that for every integer $i\ge 0$ and every thickening $t\ge 1$, the localized cohomology module
\[
\operatorname{H}^i\big(X_t,\, \mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a
\]
is flat as an $A_a$-module.
B. There exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ such that for every integer $i\ge 0$ and every thickening $t\ge 1$, the localized cohomology module
\[
\operatorname{H}^i\big(X_t,\, \mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a
\]
is a free $A_a$-module.
C. There exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ such that for every thickening $t\ge 1$, the localized cohomology module
\[
\operatorname{H}^0\big(X_t,\, \mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a
\]
is flat as an $A_a$-module.
D. There exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ such that for every integer $i\ge 0$ and every thickening $t\ge 1$, the localized cohomology module
\[
\operatorname{H}^i\big(X_t,\, \mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a
\]
is flat as an $A_a$-module, and for each fixed $i$ its rank over $A_a$ is independent of $t$.
E. There exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ such that for every integer $i\ge 0$, there is an integer $t_0=t_0(i)\ge 1$ with the property that for all $t\ge t_0$, the natural restriction map
\[
\operatorname{H}^i\big(X_{t+1},\, \mathcal O_{X_{t+1}}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a\longrightarrow \operatorname{H}^i\big(X_t,\, \mathcal O_{X_t}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}} \mathcal F\big)\otimes_A A_a
\]
is an isomorphism.

Let \(\mathcal H\in(\tfrac13,1)\). Work on the torus \(\mathbb T^d\), and let \(u^\epsilon,w^\epsilon,r^\epsilon:\mathbb T^d\times[0,T]\to\mathbb R^d\) be divergence-free, zero-mean vector fields. Let \(W_t^{\mathcal H}\) be a divergence-free \(\mathcal H\)-fractional Wiener process on \([L^2(\mathbb T^d)]^d\) with covariance operator \(Q\). Write \(A\) for the Laplacian/Stokes operator on divergence-free fields and \(b(a,c)=a\cdot\nabla c\). For each \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\), let \(u_0^\epsilon,v_0^\epsilon\) be divergence-free, zero-mean initial data satisfying
\[
\sup_{\epsilon\in(0,1)}\bigl(\|u_0^\epsilon\|_{L_x^2}+\|\sqrt\epsilon\,v_0^\epsilon\|_{L_x^2}\bigr)<\infty,
\]
and assume that the operators \(Q\) and \(C\) satisfy the required hypotheses. Consider the \(\epsilon\)-dependent system
\[
\partial_t u^{\epsilon}=\nu A u^{\epsilon}-b\bigl(u^{\epsilon}+\epsilon^{-\alpha+\mathcal H}w^{\epsilon}+r^{\epsilon},u^{\epsilon}\bigr),
\]
\[
dw^{\epsilon}=\epsilon^{-1}Cw^{\epsilon}\,dt+\epsilon^{-\mathcal H}dW_t^{\mathcal H},
\]
\[
\partial_t r^{\epsilon}=\epsilon^{-1}Cr^{\epsilon}+\nu A\bigl(\epsilon^{-\alpha+\mathcal H}w^{\epsilon}+r^{\epsilon}\bigr)-b\bigl(u^{\epsilon}+\epsilon^{-\alpha+\mathcal H}w^{\epsilon}+r^{\epsilon},\epsilon^{-\alpha+\mathcal H}w^{\epsilon}+r^{\epsilon}\bigr),
\]
with initial conditions \(u^{\epsilon}(0)=u_0^\epsilon\), \(w^{\epsilon}(0)=0\), and \(r^{\epsilon}(0)=v_0^\epsilon\). Here, a probabilistically weak rough path solution means a weak-in-law solution together with its driving rough path. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of probabilistically weak rough path solutions and their limiting behavior as \(\epsilon\to0\)?

Options:
A. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
B. There exists a family of probabilistically weak rough path solutions \(\{(u^{\epsilon},(-C)^{-1}dW^{\mathcal H,\epsilon})\}_{\epsilon\in(0,1)}\) to the above system that converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
du=\left(\nu \Delta u-u\cdot\nabla u\right)dt+d\nabla p-dW^{\mathcal H}\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\alpha=1\) and \(\mathcal H>\tfrac12\), and converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
\partial_t u=\nu \Delta u-\overline r\cdot\nabla u-u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla p,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\mathcal H<\tfrac12\) and \(\alpha=\tfrac12+\mathcal H\), where \(\overline r\) denotes the It\^o--Stokes drift.
C. There exists a family of probabilistically weak rough path solutions \(\{(u^{\epsilon},(-C)^{-1}dW^{\mathcal H,\epsilon})\}_{\epsilon\in(0,1)}\) to the above system that converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
du=\left(\nu \Delta u-u\cdot\nabla u\right)dt+d\nabla p-d(-C)^{-1}W^{\mathcal H}\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\alpha=1\) and \(\mathcal H>\tfrac12\), and converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
\partial_t u=\nu \Delta u+\overline r\cdot\nabla u-u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla p,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\mathcal H<\tfrac12\) and \(\alpha=\tfrac12+\mathcal H\), where \(\overline r\) denotes the It\^o--Stokes drift.
D. There exists a family of probabilistically weak rough path solutions \(\{(u^{\epsilon},(-C)^{-1}dW^{\mathcal H,\epsilon})\}_{\epsilon\in(0,1)}\) to the above system that converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
du=\left(\nu \Delta u-u\cdot\nabla u\right)dt+d\nabla p-d(-C)^{-1}W^{\mathcal H}\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\alpha=1\) and \(\mathcal H>\tfrac12\), and converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
du=\left(\nu \Delta u-u\cdot\nabla u\right)dt+d\nabla p-d(-C)^{-1}W^{\mathcal H}\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
in the case \(\mathcal H<\tfrac12\) and \(\alpha=\tfrac12+\mathcal H\).
E. There exists a family of probabilistically weak rough path solutions \(\{(u^{\epsilon},(-C)^{-1}dW^{\mathcal H,\epsilon})\}_{\epsilon\in(0,1)}\) to the above system such that, in the case \(\mathcal H<\tfrac12\) and \(\alpha=\tfrac12+\mathcal H\), the family converges in law to a probabilistically weak rough path solution of
\[
\partial_t u=\nu \Delta u-\overline r\cdot\nabla u-u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla p,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
where \(\overline r\) denotes the It\^o--Stokes drift.

Let $3\le n\le 5$, and let $\Sigma^n\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a two-sided embedded minimal disk (i.e. an embedded minimal hypersurface diffeomorphic to the $n$-dimensional unit disk, with a globally defined unit normal) with $\sup_{\Sigma}|A|<\infty$, where $|A|$ is the norm of the second fundamental form. For $x\in\Sigma$, write $\mathcal{B}_r(x)$ for the intrinsic geodesic ball in $\Sigma$ of radius $r$ (with respect to the induced metric), and write $B_R(x)$ for the Euclidean ball in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ of radius $R$. If $\Sigma_{x,R}$ denotes the connected component of $B_R(x)\cap \Sigma$ containing $x$, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the containment of $\Sigma_{x,R}$ in an intrinsic geodesic ball under these assumptions?

Options:
A. There exists a constant $c=c\bigl(n,\sup_{\Sigma}|A|\bigr)>0$ such that for every $x\in\Sigma$ and every $R>1$ with $\mathcal{B}_R(x)\subset \Sigma$, one has
\[
B_R(x)\cap \Sigma\subset \mathcal{B}_{cR^n}(x).
\]
B. There exists a constant $c=c\bigl(n,\sup_{\Sigma}|A|\bigr)>0$ such that for every $x\in\Sigma$ and every $R>1$, one has
\[
\Sigma_{x,R}\subset \mathcal{B}_{cR^n}(x).
\]
C. There exists a function $\rho:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, depending only on $n$ and $\sup_{\Sigma}|A|$, such that for every $x\in\Sigma$ and every $R>1$ with $\mathcal{B}_R(x)\subset \Sigma$, one has
\[
\Sigma_{x,R}\subset \mathcal{B}_{\rho(R)}(x).
\]
D. There exists a constant $c=c(n)>0$ such that for every $x\in\Sigma$ and every $R>1$ with $\mathcal{B}_R(x)\subset \Sigma$, one has
\[
\Sigma_{x,R}\subset \mathcal{B}_{cR^n}(x).
\]
E. There exists a constant $c=c\bigl(n,\sup_{\Sigma}|A|\bigr)>0$ such that for every $x\in\Sigma$ and every $R>1$ with $\mathcal{B}_R(x)\subset \Sigma$, one has
\[
\Sigma_{x,R}\subset \mathcal{B}_{cR^n}(x).
\]

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, let $E\subset\Omega$ be measurable, fix constants $0<\alpha<\beta<+\infty$, and set
\[
\sigma_E:=\beta\,\mathbbm{1}_E+\alpha\,\mathbbm{1}_{E^c},
\]
where $\mathbbm{1}_E$ denotes the characteristic function of $E$. Let $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ be a local minimizer of the functional
\[
\mathcal F(v;E)=\int_{\Omega} \sigma_E(x)\,F(\nabla v)\,dx,
\]
meaning that for every ball $B_r(x_0)\subset\Omega$ and every $\phi\in W^{1,p}_0(B_r(x_0))$ one has
\[
\mathcal F(u;B_r(x_0))\le \mathcal F(u+\phi;B_r(x_0)).
\]
Assume that $\partial E$ is a hypersurface of class $C^1$, that the structural assumptions $(H1)$--$(H2)$ hold, and that $2<p<\frac{2n}{n-2}$. Fix $0\le \lambda<n$. Here $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$ means that $\Omega'$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$, and $L^{p,\lambda}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ means membership in $L^{p,\lambda}(\Omega')$ for every such $\Omega'$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the Morrey-space regularity of $\nabla u$ under these assumptions?

Options:
A. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
B. For every $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, there exists a constant
$C=C\big(n,p,\nu,L,\beta,E,\operatorname{diam}(\Omega),\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)\big)>0$
such that
\[
\|\nabla u\|_{L^{p,0}(\Omega')}\le C.
\]
In particular, $\nabla u\in L^{p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.
C. For every $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, there exists a constant
$C=C\big(n,p,\nu,L,\beta,\operatorname{diam}(\Omega),\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)\big)>0$
such that
\[
\|\nabla u\|_{L^{p,\lambda}(\Omega')}\le C.
\]
In particular, $\nabla u\in L^{p,\lambda}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.
D. For every $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, there exists a constant
$C=C\big(n,p,\nu,L,\beta,E,\operatorname{diam}(\Omega),\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)\big)>0$
such that
\[
\|\nabla u\|_{L^{q,\lambda}(\Omega')}\le C
\qquad\text{for every }q\in[p,sp],
\]
where $s>1$ is the higher-integrability exponent. In particular, $\nabla u\in L^{q,\lambda}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for every $q\in[p,sp]$.
E. There exists a constant
$C=C\big(n,p,\nu,L,\beta,E,\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)\big)>0$
such that
\[
\|\nabla u\|_{L^{p,\lambda}(\Omega)}\le C.
\]
In particular, $\nabla u\in L^{p,\lambda}(\Omega)$.

Let \(\Omega\Subset \mathbb C^n\) be a strictly pseudoconvex domain. For a Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), define its relative capacity by
\[
cap(E,\Omega)=\sup\left\{\int_E (dd^c u)^n: u\in PSH(\Omega),\ -1\le u\le 0\right\},
\]
and define
\[
{\tt c}(E)=\inf\left\{\|v\|_*^2: v\in W^*(\Omega),\ v\le 0,\ \{v\le -1\}^o\supset E\right\},
\]
where \(\{v\le -1\}^o\supset E\) means that \(v\le -1\) almost everywhere in a neighborhood of \(E\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the uniform comparison between \({\tt c}(E)\) and \(cap(E,\Omega)\)?

Options:
A. There exists a constant \(A>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[{\tt c}(E)\le A\,[cap(E,\Omega)]^{1/n}.\] Moreover, for every subdomain \(D\Subset \Omega\), there exists a constant \(A'>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset D\), \[\frac{1}{A'}\,cap(E,\Omega)\le {\tt c}(E).\]
B. There exists a constant \(A>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[{\tt c}(E)\le A\,[cap(E,\Omega)]^{1/n}.\] Moreover, for every subdomain \(D\Subset \Omega\), there exists a constant \(A'>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset D\), \[\frac{1}{A'}\,cap(E,D)\le {\tt c}(E).\]
C. There exists a constant \(A>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[{\tt c}(E)\le A\,[cap(E,\Omega)]^{1/n}.\] Moreover, there exists a constant \(A'>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[\frac{1}{A'}\,cap(E,\Omega)\le {\tt c}(E).\]
D. There exists a constant \(A>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[{\tt c}(E)\le A\,[cap(E,\Omega)]^{1/n}.\]
E. There exists a constant \(A>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset \Omega\), \[{\tt c}(E)\le A\,cap(E,\Omega).\] Moreover, for every subdomain \(D\Subset \Omega\), there exists a constant \(A'>0\) such that for every Borel set \(E\subset D\), \[\frac{1}{A'}\,cap(E,\Omega)\le {\tt c}(E).\]

Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold with a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$, and let $S\subset M$ be a closed connected surface that is almost transverse to $\varphi$ but is not a fiber (that is, not a fiber of a fibration $M\to S^1$). Let $c^s$ and $c^u$ be the stable and unstable multicurves of $S$, namely the essential multicurves coming from the closed leaves of the singular foliations on $S$ induced by the stable/unstable foliations of $\varphi$. Write $M\!\backslash\!\backslash S$ for the manifold obtained by cutting $M$ open along $S$, and assume the numerical invariant $\mathfrak c(M\!\backslash\!\backslash S)$ is finite. Here $d_{\mathcal C(S)}$ denotes distance in the curve complex of $S$, $\mathrm{vol}(M)$ is the hyperbolic volume of $M$, and $\ell_M(\gamma)$ is the hyperbolic length of a closed geodesic $\gamma\subset M$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the uniform existence of bounds for $d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u)$ in terms of $\mathrm{vol}(M)$ and $\ell_M(\gamma)$ under these assumptions?

Options:
A. There is a constant \(k_S = k_S(\chi(S)) \ge 1\), depending only on \(\chi(S)\), and a constant \(k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S} \ge 1\), depending only on \(\chi(S)\) and \(\mathfrak c(M\backslash\!\!\backslash S)\), so that the following inequalities hold: \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\mathrm{vol}(M)+k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S}\), and \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\ell_M(\gamma)+k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S}\) for every closed geodesic \(\gamma\subset M\), whether or not \(\gamma\) intersects \(S\) essentially.

There is a constant \(k_S = k_S(\chi(S)) \ge 1\), depending only on \(\chi(S)\), and a constant \(k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S} \ge 1\), depending only on \(\chi(S)\) and \(\mathfrak c(M\backslash\!\!\backslash S)\), so that the following inequalities hold: \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\mathrm{vol}(M)\), and \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\ell_M(\gamma)+k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S}\) whenever \(\gamma\) is a closed geodesic that intersects \(S\) essentially.

There is a constant \(k_S = k_S(\chi(S)) \ge 1\), depending only on \(\chi(S)\), and a constant \(k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S} \ge 1\), depending only on \(\mathfrak c(M\backslash\!\!\backslash S)\), so that the following inequalities hold: \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\mathrm{vol}(M)+k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S}\), and \(d_{\mathcal C(S)}(c^s,c^u) \le k_S\,\ell_M(\gamma)+k_{M\backslash\!\!\backslash S}\) whenever \(\gamma\) is a closed geodesic that intersects \(S\) essentially.

Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, and let $\gamma\subset M$ be a simple closed geodesic of length $\ell$. Assume that $\gamma$ has an embedded tubular neighborhood, with respect to the hyperbolic metric on $M$, of radius at least $R$, where $R\in(0,1)$. The complement $M-\gamma$ carries a unique hyperbolic metric. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate for $\operatorname{vol}(M-\gamma)$, with a constant independent of $M$, $\gamma$, $\ell$, and $R$?

Options:
A. There exists a constant $c>0$ such that for every such $M$, $\gamma$, $\ell$, and $R\in(0,1)$, one has
\[

\]
B. There exists a constant $c>0$ such that for every such $M$, $\gamma$, $\ell$, and $R\in(0,1)$, one has

\operatorname{vol}(M-\gamma)\le \operatorname{vol}(M)+c\frac{\ell}{R}.
\]

\operatorname{vol}(M-\gamma)\le \operatorname{vol}(M)+c_\rho\ell.
\]

\]

Let $G$ be a maximal $K_5$-minor-free graph, meaning that $G$ has no $K_5$ minor and adding any missing edge to $G$ creates a $K_5$ minor. Here a $2$-sum or $3$-sum means identifying two graphs along a common clique of size $2$ or $3$, respectively; a maximal planar graph is a planar graph to which no edge can be added while preserving planarity; and $M_8$ denotes the $8$-vertex Möbius ladder. Let $p\ge 1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ denote the Schwartz class on $\mathbb R^2$, and let $\|\cdot\|_p$ denote the usual $L^p(\mathbb R^2)$ norm. For $t>0$, define the circular averaging operators
\[
A_t f(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(x_1-t\cos\alpha,\,x_2-t\sin\alpha)\,d\alpha,
\]
and let $V_2^I A f$ denote the $2$-variation in the parameter $t$ over a fixed interval $I$ of the family $\{A_t f\}_{t\in I}$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about $V_2^I A f$ acting on $f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$?

Options:
A. For every $p>2$ there exist constants $C_p<\infty$ and $\lambda_0(p)\ge 1$ such that, whenever $\lambda\ge \lambda_0(p)$ and $f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfies $\|f\|_p\le 1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\widehat f\subseteq \{\xi\in\mathbb R^2:|\xi|\le \lambda\}$, one has
\[
\|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_p\,(\log \lambda)^{\frac14-\frac1{2p}}.
\]
B. For every $p>2$, 
\[
\sup_{\substack{f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)\\ \|f\|_p\le 1}} \|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}=\infty,
\]
whereas for every $1\le p\le 2$ one has
\[
\sup_{\substack{f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)\\ \|f\|_p\le 1}} \|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}<\infty.
\]
C. Whenever $I$ is a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, the smooth dependence of $A_t f$ on $t$ implies that for every $p\ge 1$ there is a constant $C_{p,I}<\infty$ such that
\[
\|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_{p,I}\,\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}
\quad\text{for all }f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2).
\]
D. For every $p\ge 1$, \[\sup_{\substack{f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)\\ \|f\|_p\le 1}} \|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}=\infty.\]
E. For every $p>2$, 
\[
\sup_{\substack{f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)\\ \|f\|_p\le 1}} \|V_2^I A f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}=\infty.
\]

In the continuum scale-free percolation model, let \(V\) be a unit-intensity homogeneous Poisson point process on \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Each \(x\in V\) carries an i.i.d. weight \(W_x\) with \(\mathbb{P}(W>w)=w^{-\beta}\) for \(w\ge 1\), and, conditional on \(V\) and the weights, distinct vertices \(x,y\) are connected independently with probability \(p_{xy}=1-\exp\{-\lambda W_xW_y/|x-y|^\alpha\}\), where \(|\cdot|\) is the Euclidean norm. Write \(E\) for the random edge set and \(x\leftrightarrow y\) for the event that \(x\) and \(y\) are joined by an edge. Define \(B_n=[-n,n]^d\), \(E_n=\{\{x,y\}\in E:x\in V\cap B_n\}\), \(e_n^*=\max_{\{x,y\}\in E_n}|x-y|\), and for fixed \(r>0\) let
\[
F(n,r)=\sum_{x\in V\cap B_n}\sum_{y\in V\cap B_n^c} \mathbf{1}_{\{|x-y|>r_n,\ x\leftrightarrow y\}} + \frac12\sum_{x\in V\cap B_n}\sum_{y\in V\cap B_n} \mathbf{1}_{\{|x-y|>r_n,\ x\leftrightarrow y\}},
\]
where \(r_n=c_n r\). Assume \(\min\{\alpha,\alpha\beta\}>d\) and either (a) \(0<\beta<1\) with \(\alpha\beta\in(d,2d]\) and \(c_n=C_1 n^{d/(\alpha\beta-d)}(\log n)^{1/(\alpha\beta-d)}\), or (b) \(\beta=1\) with \(\alpha\in(d,2d]\) and \(c_n=C_2 n^{d/(\alpha-d)}(\log n)^{2/(\alpha-d)}\), or (c) \(\beta>1\) with \(\alpha\in(d,2d)\) and \(c_n=C_3 n^{d/(\alpha-d)}\), where \(C_1,C_2,C_3>0\) are constants independent of \(n\). Writing \(\theta=\alpha\beta-d\) for \(0<\beta<1\) and \(\theta=\alpha-d\) for \(\beta\ge 1\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the asymptotic behavior of \(F(n,r)\) and \(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\) as \(n\to\infty\)?

Options:
A. For every \(r>0\), \(F(n,r)\) converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \(r^{-\theta}\).
B. For every \(r>0\), \(F(n,r)\) converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \(\kappa r^{-\theta}\) for some finite constant \(\kappa=\kappa(d,\alpha,\beta,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)\), and \(\mathbb{P}(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\le r)\to \exp(-\kappa r^{-\theta})\); equivalently, \(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\) has a Fr\'echet limit with parameter \(\theta\) but with a non-unit scale.
C. For every \(r>0\), \(F(n,r)\) converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \(r^{-\theta}\), and \(\mathbb{P}(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\le r)\to \exp(-r^{-\theta})\), so \(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\) converges in distribution to a Fr\'echet random variable with parameter \(\theta\); however, in the borderline regime \(\beta=1\) this conclusion requires \(\alpha\in(d,2d)\), excluding the endpoint \(\alpha=2d\).
D. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
E. For every \(r>0\), \(F(n,r)\) converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \(r^{-\theta}\), but because edges with both endpoints in \(B_n\) are counted with the factor \(1/2\), the event \(\{e_n^*\le r_n\}\) is not exactly the same as \(\{F(n,r)=0\}\); hence the Poisson limit for \(F(n,r)\) does not by itself yield the Fr\'echet limit for \(c_n^{-1}e_n^*\).

Let \(0<r<R\), let \(A=A(r,R)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: r<|z|<R\}\), and define the Cauchy transform on the annulus by
\[
(C_A f)(z)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_A \frac{f(w)}{z-w}\,dA(w),\qquad z\in A,\ f\in L^2(A),
\]
where \(dA\) denotes planar area measure. If \(J_\nu\) and \(Y_\nu\) denote the Bessel functions of the first and second kind, respectively, which statement about the \(L^2(A)\to L^2(A)\) operator norm of \(C_A\) holds?

\[

\]
where \(\lambda_1(A)\) is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) on \(A\); equivalently, \(\sqrt{\lambda_1(A)}\) is the smallest positive solution of
\[
J_0(\kappa r)Y_0(\kappa R)-J_0(\kappa R)Y_0(\kappa r)=0.
\]

\[
\|C_A\|_{L^2(A)\to L^2(A)}=\frac{2}{\kappa_1},
\]
where \(\kappa_1>0\) is the smallest positive solution of

J_1(\kappa r)Y_0(\kappa R)-Y_1(\kappa r)J_0(\kappa R)=0.
\]

\[
\|C_A\|_{L^2(A)\to L^2(A)}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\mu_1}},
\]
where \(\mu_1\) is the first eigenvalue of a mixed Neumann--Dirichlet Laplacian problem on the annulus; equivalently, \(\mu_1=\kappa_1^2\) for a smallest positive root \(\kappa_1\) of a Bessel transcendental equation depending on \(r\) and \(R\).
D. The norm is
\[
\|C_A\|_{L^2(A)\to L^2(A)}=\frac{2}{\kappa_1},
\]
where \(\kappa_1>0\) is the smallest positive solution of
\[
J_0(\kappa r)Y_1(\kappa R)-Y_0(\kappa r)J_1(\kappa R)=0.
\]
E. The norm is
\[
\|C_A\|_{L^2(A)\to L^2(A)}=\frac{2}{\kappa_1},
\]
where \(\kappa_1>0\) is the smallest positive solution of
\[
J_0(\kappa r)Y_0(\kappa R)-Y_0(\kappa r)J_0(\kappa R)=0.
\]

Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^N$ be open. Assume that there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\}$ such that
\[
\lambda_{k,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)<\mathcal{E}_p(\Omega).
\]
Here $\lambda_{\ell,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)$ denotes the $\ell$-th Lusternik--Schnirelmann minmax value, and saying that a number $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian on $\Omega$ means that there exists a nonzero $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ such that
\[
-\operatorname{div}\big(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u\big)=\lambda |u|^{p-2}u
\]
in the weak sense on $\Omega$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the minmax values $\lambda_{\ell,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)$ under these assumptions?

\[
|u_\ell(x)|\le C_\ell\,\|u_\ell\|_{L^p(\Omega)}e^{-\alpha|x|}\qquad \text{for every }\alpha>0\text{ and every }x\in\Omega.
\]

C. If there exists \(k\in\mathbb N\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(\lambda_{k,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)\le \mathcal E_p(\Omega)\), then for every \(\ell\in\{1,\dots,k\}\) the minmax value \(\lambda_{\ell,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)\) is an eigenvalue of the Dirichlet \(p\)-Laplacian on \(\Omega\).
D. If there exists \(k\in\mathbb N\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(\lambda_{k,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)<\mathcal E_p(\Omega)\), then in fact every minmax value \(\lambda_{\ell,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)\), with \(\ell\in\mathbb N\setminus\{0\}\), is an eigenvalue of the Dirichlet \(p\)-Laplacian on \(\Omega\).
E. For each \(\ell\in\{1,\dots,k\}\), there exists a nonzero \(u_\ell\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)\) such that
\[
-\operatorname{div}\big(|\nabla u_\ell|^{p-2}\nabla u_\ell\big)=\lambda_{\ell,p}^{\rm LS}(\Omega)\,|u_\ell|^{p-2}u_\ell
\]
in the weak sense on \(\Omega\).

Let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2\) be a smooth bounded convex domain with inradius \(\operatorname{inr}(\Omega)=r\) (the radius of the largest ball contained in \(\Omega\)) and diameter \(D(\Omega)=D\). \[
\begin{cases}
u_t-\Delta u=0, & (x,t)\in \Omega\times \mathbb{R}^+,\\
\partial_{\nu}u=\lambda g(u), & (x,t)\in \partial\Omega\times \mathbb{R}^+,\\
u(x,0)=u_0(x), & x\in \Omega,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\partial_{\nu}u\) denotes the outward normal derivative on \(\partial\Omega\), and a "pattern" means a non-constant stable stationary solution of this problem. Assuming the diameter \(D\) is sufficiently large, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of patterns for this problem?

E. There exists a parameter \(\lambda>0\), depending only on \(r\), such that every smooth bounded convex domain with inradius \(r\) and sufficiently large diameter admits a pattern for that same \(\lambda\).

Let \(\alpha=\frac{c}{d}\), where \(c,d,s\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) satisfy \(d\ge 2\), \(1\le c,s\le d\), and \(\gcd(cs,d)=1\). Let \(p\ge 5\) be a prime with \(p\equiv s\pmod d\). Since \(d\) is prime to \(p\), we view \(\alpha\) as a \(p\)-adic integer. For a \(p\)-adic integer \(x\), let \(\langle x\rangle_p\) denote the least nonnegative residue of \(x\) modulo \(p\), and define Dwork’s dash operation by
\[
x^*=\frac{x+\langle -x\rangle_p}{p}.
\]
Recursively, set \(x^{\ast_0}=x\) and \(x^{\ast_n}=(x^{\ast_{n-1}})^*\) for \(n\ge 1\). Assume
\[
\bigl(\tfrac12+\alpha\bigr)^{\ast_r}\bigl(\tfrac12+\alpha^{\ast_r}\bigr)\not\equiv 0\pmod p.
\]
Here \((a)_k\) denotes the Pochhammer symbol and \(H_n^{(2)}=\sum_{j=1}^n j^{-2}\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(2k+\alpha)\frac{(\alpha)_k^3\left(\tfrac12\right)_k}{(1)_k^3\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)_k}
\]
modulo \(p^{r+3}\) under these hypotheses?

Options:
A. It satisfies
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(2k+\alpha)\frac{(\alpha)_k^3\left(\tfrac12\right)_k}{(1)_k^3\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)_k}
\equiv \alpha^{\ast_r}p^r-\frac{(\alpha^{\ast_r})^3}{\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)^{\ast_r}}\,p^{r+2}H_{\alpha^{\ast_r}p-\alpha^{\ast_{r-1}}}^{(2)}
\pmod{p^{r+2}}.
\]
B. It satisfies
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(2k+\alpha)\frac{(\alpha)_k^3\left(\tfrac12\right)_k}{(1)_k^3\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)_k}
\equiv \alpha^{\ast_r}p^r-\frac{(\alpha^{\ast_r})^3}{\tfrac12+\alpha^{\ast_r}}\,p^{r+2}H_{\alpha^{\ast_r}p-\alpha^{\ast_{r-1}}}^{(2)}
\pmod{p^{r+3}}.
\]
C. It satisfies
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(2k+\alpha)\frac{(\alpha)_k^3\left(\tfrac12\right)_k}{(1)_k^3\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)_k}
\equiv \alpha^{\ast_r}p^r-\frac{(\alpha^{\ast_r})^3}{\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)^{\ast_r}}\,p^{r+2}H_{\alpha^{\ast_r}p-\alpha^{\ast_r}}^{(2)}
\pmod{p^{r+3}}.
\]
D. It satisfies
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(2k+\alpha)\frac{(\alpha)_k^3\left(\tfrac12\right)_k}{(1)_k^3\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)_k}
\equiv \alpha^{\ast_r}p^r-\frac{(\alpha^{\ast_{r-1}})^3}{\left(\tfrac12+\alpha\right)^{\ast_r}}\,p^{r+2}H_{\alpha^{\ast_r}p-\alpha^{\ast_{r-1}}}^{(2)}
\pmod{p^{r+3}}.
\]
E. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

Let \((\mathcal M_1,g_1)\) and \((\mathcal M_2,g_2)\) be two smooth connected \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with boundary. Let \(\omega_1\subset \mathcal M_1\) and \(\omega_2\subset \mathcal M_2\) be open connected subsets. For each \(j=1,2\), let \(L^2\Omega^1(\omega_j)\) denote the space of square-integrable 1-forms on \(\omega_j)\), and define the local source-to-final value map
\[
\mathcal N_j:\mathbb B_\delta\to L^2\Omega^1(\omega_j),\qquad \mathcal N_j(\mathbf f)=\mathbf u_{\mathbf f}(T,\cdot)|_{\omega_j},
\]
where \(\mathbb B_\delta\) is a small ball of admissible source 1-forms, and \(\mathbf u_{\mathbf f}\) is the corresponding solution of the geometric Navier--Stokes system on \([0,T]\times \mathcal M_j\) with zero initial and boundary data, evaluated at the final time \(T\). Assume there exists a diffeomorphism \(\Phi:\omega_1\to\omega_2\) such that, with \(\Phi^*\) denoting pullback on the relevant source and final-value 1-forms,
\[
\mathcal N_1\,\Phi^*=\Phi^*\,\mathcal N_2.
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about \((\mathcal M_1,g_1)\) and \((\mathcal M_2,g_2)\) under these assumptions?

Options:
A. The diffeomorphism \(\Phi\) extends to a global isometry \(\widetilde\Phi:\mathcal M_1\to\mathcal M_2\), and after identifying the manifolds by \(\widetilde\Phi\) the full nonlinear source-to-final value maps agree for all admissible \(L^2\)-source 1-forms, not merely for sources in the small ball \(\mathbb B_\delta\).
B. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
C. The intertwining identity implies equality, via \(\Phi\), of the localized spectral projections for the stationary Stokes operator on \(\omega_1\) and \(\omega_2\); however, this determines at most the domains of influence of the observation sets up to time \(T\), not the full manifolds up to isometry.
D. There exists a sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), depending only on \(T\), such that intertwining on \(\mathbb B_\delta\) identifies the linearized Stokes dynamics on \(\omega_1\) and \(\omega_2\); to deduce that \((\mathcal M_1,g_1)\) and \((\mathcal M_2,g_2)\) are globally isometric one would need the additional hypothesis that \(T\) exceed the relevant geometric controllability time.
E. The intertwining identity already forces the first-order linearizations of \(\mathcal N_1\) and \(\mathcal N_2\) at \(0\) to agree under \(\Phi\); equivalently, the local source-to-final maps for the corresponding linearized Stokes systems coincide on the observation regions, which is weaker than global isometry.

Let $2\le p<\infty$, $0<s<1$, and $0\le \Lambda\le 1$. Assume $\Omega\subset \mathbb H^n$ is a bounded open set and $u\in HW^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\cap L^{p-1}_{sp}(\mathbb H^n)$ is a weak solution of
\[
-\Delta_{\mathbb H,p}u+\Lambda(-\Delta_{\mathbb H,p})^s u=0\quad\text{in }\Omega.
\]
Here $Q=2n+2$ is the homogeneous dimension of $\mathbb H^n$. For $\xi_0\in\mathbb H^n$, let $B_r(\xi_0)=\{\xi\in\mathbb H^n:\ \|\xi_0^{-1}\circ \xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}<r\}$ be the Kor\'anyi ball, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb H^n}$ is the Kor\'anyi gauge. Also define
\[
\operatorname{Tail}_{q,\alpha,\beta}(u;\xi_0,R)=\left[R^\beta\int_{\mathbb H^n\setminus B_R(\xi_0)}\frac{|u(\xi)|^q}{\|\xi_0^{-1}\circ \xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{Q+\alpha}}\,d\xi\right]^{1/q}.
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative local H\"older estimate for every $0<\gamma<1$ and every Kor\'anyi ball $B_{2R}(\xi_0)\Subset\Omega$ with $0<R<1$?

Options:
A. There exists a constant $c=c(Q,p,s,\gamma)>0$ such that
\[
\sup_{\xi\ne\eta\in B_{R/2}(\xi_0)}\frac{|u(\xi)-u(\eta)|}{\|\eta^{-1}\circ\xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{\gamma}}
\le \frac{c}{R^{\gamma}}\left(\|u\|_{L^\infty(B_R(\xi_0))}+\operatorname{Tail}_{p-1,sp,sp}(u;\xi_0,R)\right).
\]
B. For every $0<\gamma<1$ and every Kor\'anyi ball $B_{2R}(\xi_0)\Subset\Omega$ with $0<R<1$, there exists a finite constant $C=C(u,\xi_0,R,Q,p,s,\gamma)$ such that
\[
|u(\xi)-u(\eta)|\le C\,\|\eta^{-1}\circ\xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{\gamma}
\qquad\text{for all }\xi,\eta\in B_{R/2}(\xi_0).
\]
C. There exists a constant $c=c(Q,p,s,\gamma)>0$ such that
\[
\sup_{\xi\ne\eta\in B_{R/2}(\xi_0)}\frac{|u(\xi)-u(\eta)|}{\|\eta^{-1}\circ\xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{\gamma}}
\le \frac{c}{R^{\gamma}}\left(\|u\|_{L^\infty(B_R(\xi_0))}+\operatorname{Tail}_{p-1,sp,p}(u;\xi_0,R)\right).
\]
D. There exists a constant $c=c(Q,p,s)>0$ such that for every $0<\gamma<1$,
\[
\sup_{\xi\ne\eta\in B_{R/2}(\xi_0)}\frac{|u(\xi)-u(\eta)|}{\|\eta^{-1}\circ\xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{\gamma}}
\le \frac{c}{R^{\gamma}}\left(\|u\|_{L^\infty(B_R(\xi_0))}+\operatorname{Tail}_{p-1,sp,p}(u;\xi_0,R)\right).
\]
E. There exists a constant $c=c(Q,p,s,\gamma)>0$ such that
\[
\sup_{\xi\ne\eta\in B_R(\xi_0)}\frac{|u(\xi)-u(\eta)|}{\|\eta^{-1}\circ\xi\|_{\mathbb H^n}^{\gamma}}
\le \frac{c}{R^{\gamma}}\left(\|u\|_{L^\infty(B_R(\xi_0))}+\operatorname{Tail}_{p-1,sp,p}(u;\xi_0,R)\right).
\]

Let \(F\subset S^3\) be a closed surface, and let \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) be the two components of \(S^3\setminus F\). Define the Heegaard deficiency of \(F\) by
\[
\delta(F)=g(M_1)+g(M_2)-g(F),

Assume \(D,S\in C^3([0,\infty))\) satisfy \(D(s)>0\) on \([0,\infty)\), \(S(s)>0\) on \((0,\infty)\), \(S(0)=0\), and for some \(k_D,k_S>0\) and \(p,q\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
D(s)\le k_D s^p,\qquad S(s)\ge k_S s^q\qquad (s\ge 1),
\]
with
\[
q-p>2-\frac n2,\qquad q>1-\frac n2.
\]
Consider the corresponding radially symmetric homogeneous Neumann problem on \(\Omega\), with positive radially symmetric initial data \(u_0,w_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\overline\Omega)\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about a uniform threshold conclusion for the initial data?

Options:
A. There exist constants \(m_1,m_2>0\) such that for every positive radially symmetric \(u_0,w_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\overline\Omega)\) satisfying
\[
\int_{\Omega} u_0\,dx\ge m_1,\qquad \int_{\Omega} w_0\,dx\ge m_2,
\]
the corresponding problem admits a classical solution on \(\Omega\times(0,T_{\max})\), and this solution blows up in finite time.
B. There exist continuous functions \(M_1,M_2\in C^0([0,R])\) and a time \(T_*>0\) such that for every positive radially symmetric \(u_0,w_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\overline\Omega)\) satisfying
\[
\int_{B_r(0)} u_0\,dx\ge M_1(r),\qquad \int_{B_r(0)} w_0\,dx\ge M_2(r)\qquad (0<r<R),
\]
the corresponding problem admits a classical solution on \(\Omega\times(0,T_{\max})\), and in fact \(T_{\max}\le T_*\).
C. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
D. There exist continuous functions \(M_1,M_2\in C^0([0,R])\) such that for every positive radially symmetric \(u_0,w_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\overline\Omega)\) satisfying
\[
\int_{B_r(0)} u_0\,dx\ge M_1(r)\qquad (0<r<R),
\]
and
\[
\int_{\Omega} w_0\,dx\ge M_2(R),
\]
the corresponding problem admits a classical solution on \(\Omega\times(0,T_{\max})\), and this solution blows up in finite time.
E. There exist continuous functions \(M_1,M_2\in C^0([0,R])\) such that for every positive radially symmetric \(u_0,w_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\overline\Omega)\) satisfying
\[
\int_{B_r(0)} u_0\,dx\ge M_1(r),\qquad \int_{B_r(0)} w_0\,dx\ge M_2(r)\qquad (0<r<R),
\]
the corresponding problem admits a classical solution on \(\Omega\times(0,T_{\max})\), where \(T_{\max}\in(0,\infty]\) denotes the maximal existence time.

For a cubic field (that is, a degree-3 number field) $K$, let $\Delta_K$ denote its discriminant and $h(K)$ its class number. Fix once and for all either the plus sign or the minus sign, so that $\pm\Delta_K$ means $+\Delta_K$ throughout or $-\Delta_K$ throughout according to that choice; also fix a real number $\varepsilon>0$ and positive integers $k$ and $H$, and let $\kappa$ be the fixed constant appearing in the exponent below. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence, for all sufficiently large $X$, of positive integers $d\le X$ satisfying the corresponding uniform conditions on the values $d+1,d+2,\dots,d+k$?

Options:
A. There exists a positive constant $c$ depending on $\pm,\varepsilon,k,H$ such that for all sufficiently large $X$, there are at least $cX^{1-\kappa-\varepsilon}$ positive integers $d\le X$ such that the following hold: for each $1\le i\le k$, if there exists a cubic field $K$ with $\pm\Delta_K=d+i$, then $h(K)>H$; and moreover
\[
\#\{K\text{ cubic field}\mid \pm\Delta_K\in\{d+1,d+2,\dots,d+k\}\}\ge \frac{k+1}{2}.
\]
B. There exists a positive constant $c$ depending on $\pm,\varepsilon,k,H$ such that for all sufficiently large $X$, there are at least $cX^{1-\kappa-\varepsilon}$ positive integers $d\le X$ such that the following hold: for each $1\le i\le k$, if there exists a cubic field $K$ with $\pm\Delta_K=d+i$, then $h(K)>H$; and moreover
\[
\#\{n\in\{d+1,d+2,\dots,d+k\}\mid n\text{ is a cubic discriminant with sign }\pm\}\ge \frac{k}{2}.
\]
C. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
D. There exists a positive constant $c$ depending on $\pm,\varepsilon,k,H$ such that for all sufficiently large $X$, there are at least $cX^{1-\kappa-\varepsilon}$ positive integers $d\le X$ for which, for each $1\le i\le k$, if there exists a cubic field $K$ with $\pm\Delta_K=d+i$, then $h(K)>H$.
E. There exists a positive constant $c$ depending on $\pm,\varepsilon,k,H$ such that for all sufficiently large $X$, there are at least $cX^{1-\kappa}$ positive integers $d\le X$ such that the following hold: for each $1\le i\le k$, if there exists a cubic field $K$ with $\pm\Delta_K=d+i$, then $h(K)>H$; and moreover
\[
\#\{K\text{ cubic field}\mid \pm\Delta_K\in\{d+1,d+2,\dots,d+k\}\}\ge \frac{k}{2}.
\]

Let \(N\ge 1\), let \(m\) satisfy \(\frac{(N-2)_+}{N+2}<m<1\) (where \((N-2)_+:=\max\{N-2,0\}\)), let \(\beta>0\), and assume the chemotactic flux has the form \(\chi(u,v)u=\chi u^{\mathfrak q-1}\) for some constant \(\chi>0\) and some exponent \(1<\mathfrak q<\frac{(m+1)(N+2)}{2N}\). Let \((u,v)\) satisfy the system
\[
\begin{cases}
u_t = \operatorname{div}(\nabla u^m)-\operatorname{div}(\chi(u,v)u\nabla v),\\[4pt]
v_t = \Delta v-\beta v+u,
\end{cases}
\qquad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty),
\]
with initial data \(u(x,0)=u_0(x)>0\) and \(v(x,0)=v_0(x)\ge 0\) on \(\mathbb{R}^N\), and assume that \(u\) is a locally bounded weak solution of the first equation. Fix \(T>0\), let \({\mathcal K}\subset \mathbb{R}^N\) be compact, and write \(\|u\|_\infty\) for the essential supremum of \(u\) on the region under consideration. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate for \(u\) on \({\mathcal K}\times(0,T]\)?

Options:
A. There exist constants \(\gamma>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), depending only on the data, such that for every compact set \({\mathcal K}\subset \mathbb{R}^N\), all \(x_1,x_2\in {\mathcal K}\), and every \(t\in(0,T]\),
\[
|u(x_1,t)-u(x_2,t)|\le \gamma |x_1-x_2|^{\theta}.
\]
B. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
C. There exist constants \(\gamma>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), depending only on the data, such that for every compact set \({\mathcal K}\subset \mathbb{R}^N\) and all \((x_1,t_1),(x_2,t_2)\in {\mathcal K}\times(0,T]\),
\[
|u(x_1,t_1)-u(x_2,t_2)|\le \gamma\Big(|x_1-x_2|+\|u\|_\infty^{\frac{m-1}{2}}|t_1-t_2|^{\frac{1}{m+1}}\Big)^{\theta}.
\]
D. There exist constants \(\gamma>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), depending only on the data, such that for every compact set \({\mathcal K}\subset \mathbb{R}^N\) and all \((x_1,t_1),(x_2,t_2)\in {\mathcal K}\times[0,T]\),
\[
|u(x_1,t_1)-u(x_2,t_2)|\le \gamma\Big(|x_1-x_2|+\|u\|_\infty^{\frac{m-1}{2}}|t_1-t_2|^{1/2}\Big)^{\theta}.
\]
E. There exist constants \(\gamma>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), depending only on the data, such that for every compact set \({\mathcal K}\subset \mathbb{R}^N\) and all \((x_1,t_1),(x_2,t_2)\in {\mathcal K}\times(0,T]\),
\[
|u(x_1,t_1)-u(x_2,t_2)|\le \gamma\Big(|x_1-x_2|+\|u\|_\infty^{\frac{1-m}{2}}|t_1-t_2|^{1/2}\Big)^{\theta}.
\]

Let \(p\) be an odd prime, let \(\mathbb F_p\) be the field of \(p\) elements, and let \(c\) be an extra vertex not in \(\mathbb F_p\). For \(x\in \mathbb F_p\), call \(x\) a quadratic residue if \(x=a^2\) for some \(a\in \mathbb F_p\), and a quadratic non-residue otherwise among \(\mathbb F_p^*=\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0\}\); regard \(0\) as a quadratic residue and \(c\) as a quadratic non-residue. A 1-factor of \(K_{p+1}\) is a perfect matching on the vertex set \(\mathbb F_p \cup \{c\}\). For an edge \(\{x,y\}\) with \(x,y\in \mathbb F_p\), define its length to be \(\min\{(x-y) \bmod p,(y-x) \bmod p\}\), where residues modulo \(p\) are taken in \(\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}\); for an edge \(\{x,c\}\), define its length to be \(0\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about 1-factors of \(K_{p+1}\) for every odd prime \(p\) under the condition that every edge joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue?

Options:
A. For every odd prime \(p\), every 1-factor \(F\) of \(K_{p+1}\) with vertex set \(\mathbb F_p \cup \{c\}\) such that every edge of \(F\) joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue already has pairwise distinct lengths.
B. There exists a 1-factor \(F\) of \(K_{p+1}\) with vertex set \(\mathbb F_p \cup \{c\}\) such that every edge of \(F\) joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue, the lengths of the edges in \(F\) are pairwise distinct, and for each \(t\in\mathbb F_p\), the matching obtained from \(F\) by replacing each finite vertex \(x\) with \(x+t\) modulo \(p\) and fixing \(c\) also has every edge joining a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue.
C. There exists a 1-factor \(F\) of \(K_{p+1}\) with vertex set \(\mathbb F_p \cup \{c\}\) such that every edge of \(F\) joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue, and the lengths of the edges in \(F\) are pairwise distinct.
D. There exists a 1-factor \(F\) of \(K_{p+1}\) with vertex set \(\mathbb F_p \cup \{c\}\) such that every edge of \(F\) joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue.
E. For every odd prime \(p\), whenever \(F\) is a 1-factor of \(K_{p+1}\) such that every edge of \(F\) joins a quadratic residue to a quadratic non-residue and the lengths of the edges in \(F\) are pairwise distinct, the unique edge of \(F\) incident to \(c\) must be \(\{c,0\}\).

Let \((M,g)\) be a complete noncompact \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold such that \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge \lambda g\) for some \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(\operatorname{inj}(M,g)\ge i>0\). For \(u\in W^{1,n}(M)\), define \(\|u\|_{1,\tau}:=\|\nabla_g u\|_{L^n(M)}+\tau\|u\|_{L^n(M)}\), let \(\phi_n(t)=e^t-\sum_{k=0}^{n-2} t^k/k!\), let \(\alpha_n=n\omega_{n-1}^{1/(n-1)}\) where \(\omega_{n-1}\) is the surface measure of the unit sphere \(S^{n-1}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(dV_g\) denote the Riemannian volume element, and let \(r_H\) denote the harmonic radius of \((M,g)\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the associated Moser--Trudinger functional on \(M\)?

Options:
A. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
B. There exists a constant \(\epsilon=\epsilon(\lambda,i,n)>0\), with \(\epsilon=O(1/r_H)\), such that for every \(\tau>\epsilon\) there is a constant \(C=C(n,\tau,\lambda,i)\), independent of the particular manifold \(M\), for which
\[
\sup_{u\in W^{1,n}(M),\ \|u\|_{1,\tau}\le 1}\int_M \phi_n\!\left(\alpha_n |u|^{\frac{n}{n-1}}\right)\,dV_g\le C.
\]
Moreover, the constant \(\alpha_n\) is sharp.
C. There exists a constant \(\epsilon=\epsilon(\lambda,i,n)>0\), with \(\epsilon=O(1/r_H)\), such that for every \(\tau>\epsilon\) there is a constant \(C=C(n,\tau,M)\) for which
\[
\sup_{u\in W^{1,n}(M),\ \|u\|_{1,\tau}\le 1}\int_M \exp\!\left(\alpha_n |u|^{\frac{n}{n-1}}\right)\,dV_g\le C.
\]
Moreover, the constant \(\alpha_n\) is sharp.
D. There exists a constant \(\epsilon=\epsilon(\lambda,i,n)>0\), with \(\epsilon=O(1/r_H)\), such that for every \(\tau>\epsilon\) and every \(0\le \alpha<\alpha_n\) there is a constant \(C=C(n,\tau,M)\) for which
\[
\sup_{u\in W^{1,n}(M),\ \|u\|_{1,\tau}\le 1}\int_M \phi_n\!\left(\alpha |u|^{\frac{n}{n-1}}\right)\,dV_g\le C.
\]
E. There exists a constant \(\epsilon=\epsilon(\lambda,i,n)>0\), with \(\epsilon=O(1/r_H)\), such that for every \(\tau>0\) there is a constant \(C=C(n,\tau,M)\) for which
\[
\sup_{u\in W^{1,n}(M),\ \|u\|_{1,\tau}\le 1}\int_M \phi_n\!\left(\alpha_n |u|^{\frac{n}{n-1}}\right)\,dV_g\le C.
\]
Moreover, the constant \(\alpha_n\) is sharp.

Let \(\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n)\) denote the normal bundle of the complex projective space \(\mathbb{CP}^n\). For a partition \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)\) of \(n\), write \(t_\lambda=t_{\lambda_1}\cdots t_{\lambda_k}\), and let \(c^\nu_\lambda(\mathbb{CP}^n)\) be the Chern number of \(\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n)\) corresponding to the monomial symmetric function \(m_\lambda\). Define the generating function
\[
C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t):=\sum_{|\lambda|=n} c^\nu_\lambda(\mathbb{CP}^n)\, t_\lambda,
\]
where \(t=(t_1,\dots,t_n)\). If \(L_n(t_1,\dots,t_n)\) denotes the \(n\)-th Lagrange inversion polynomial, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the identity satisfied by \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)\)?

Options:
A. \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)=(n+1)L_n(t_1,\dots,t_n)\).
B. \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)=(-1)^n(n+1)L_n(t_1,\dots,t_n)\).
C. \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)=(n+1)L_n\!\left(\dfrac{t_1}{2!},\dfrac{t_2}{3!},\dots,\dfrac{t_n}{(n+1)!}\right)\).
D. \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)\) is a scalar multiple of the Lagrange inversion polynomial \(L_n(t_1,\dots,t_n)\).
E. \(C^\nu(\mathbb{CP}^n,t)=(n+1)L_n(t_1,-t_2,t_3,-t_4,\dots,(-1)^{n-1}t_n)\).

Let $(G,\sigma)$ be a signed graph, meaning that each edge of the cubic graph $G$ is assigned a sign $\pm 1$. Assume that $G$ is 3-regular, that $(G,\sigma)$ is flow-admissible (that is, it admits a nowhere-zero integer flow in the usual signed-graph sense), and that it is cyclically 5-edge-connected, i.e. every edge cut whose removal separates the graph into two subgraphs each containing a cycle has size at least $5$. Here a nowhere-zero $6$-flow means a nowhere-zero integer flow whose edge values lie in $\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,\pm4,\pm5\}$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about $(G,\sigma)$?

Options:
A. Every flow-admissible, cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graph has a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_6$-flow.
B. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
C. Every cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graph has a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_6$-flow.
D. Every flow-admissible, cyclically 4-edge-connected, cubic signed graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow.
E. Every flow-admissible, cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.

Assume that the hypotheses \((f_1'), (f_2), (f_3)\) hold for the energy functional \(J\) considered on \(X=H_0^1(\Omega)\). Here, an unbounded sequence means a sequence that is not bounded in \(X\), and for a critical point \(u\), \(M(J,u)\) denotes the generalized Morse index, i.e. the sum of the dimensions of the negative and null eigenspaces of \(J''(u)\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the critical points of \(J\) under these assumptions?

Options:
A. The functional \(J\) has a sequence of critical points \(\{u_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) such that \(M(J,u_k) \to \infty\) as \(k\to\infty\).
B. The functional \(J\) has an unbounded sequence of critical points \(\{u_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) such that \(M(J,u_k) \to \infty\) and \(J(u_k) \to \infty\) as \(k \to \infty\).
C. The functional \(J\) has an unbounded sequence of critical points \(\{u_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) such that \(M(J,u_k)\ge k\) for every \(k\), and the sequence of critical values \(\{J(u_k)\}\) converges to a finite real number.
D. For each integer \(k\ge 1\), the functional \(J\) has a critical point \(u_k\) with generalized Morse index exactly \(M(J,u_k)=k\), and \(J(u_k)\to\infty\) as \(k\to\infty\).
E. The functional \(J\) has an unbounded sequence of critical points \(\{u_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) such that \(J(u_k)\to\infty\) and the dimension of the null eigenspace of \(J''(u_k)\) is at least \(k\) for every \(k\).

Let \(L\) be a link in \(S^3\) that is non-split (it cannot be separated into two nonempty parts by a 2-sphere), nontrivial (not an unlink), and not the Hopf link. Let \(c(L)\) denote the crossing number of \(L\), i.e. the minimum number of crossings in any diagram of \(L\). Let \(\alpha_3(L)\) denote the three-page index of \(L\), meaning the minimal number of arcs needed to represent \(L\) in a three-page presentation. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the explicit inequality relating \(\alpha_3(L)\) and \(c(L)\) under these hypotheses?

Options:
A. \[\alpha_3(L)\le 3c(L)-1\quad\text{for every non-split, nontrivial link }L.\]
B. \[\alpha_3(L)\le 3c(L).\]
C. \[\alpha_3(L)\le 3c(L)-1.\]
D. \[\alpha_3(L)\le 3c(L)-2.\]
E. \[\alpha_3(L)=3c(L)-1.\]

Let \(n\ge 2\) and \(0<s<1\). Let \(\mathbb H^n\) denote the \(n\)-dimensional hyperbolic space, and let \(( -\Delta_{\mathbb H^n})^s\) be the fractional Laplacian on \(\mathbb H^n\). Suppose \(u\in L^q(\mathbb H^n)\) for some \(q>p\) is a nonnegative weak solution of
\[
(-\Delta_{\mathbb H^n})^s u = u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbb H^n,
\]
meaning that for every \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb H^n)\),
\[
\int_{\mathbb H^n} u(x)(-\Delta_{\mathbb H^n})^s\varphi(x)\,dV_x
=\int_{\mathbb H^n} u(x)^p\varphi(x)\,dV_x.
\]
Here, saying that \(u\) is radially symmetric and nondecreasing about a point \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) means that \(u(x)\) depends only on the hyperbolic distance \(d_{\mathbb H^n}(x,x_0)\) and is nondecreasing as that distance increases. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about such solutions in the subcritical and critical cases \(1<p\le \frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), assuming in addition that \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\) when \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\)?

Options:
A. If \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) and \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\), then \(u\equiv 0\). If \(p=\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), then there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) such that \(u\) is radially symmetric and nondecreasing about \(x_0\).
B. If \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) and \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\), then \(u\equiv 0\). If \(p=\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), then there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) such that \(u\) is radially symmetric, nondecreasing about \(x_0\), and strictly positive on \(\mathbb H^n\).
C. If \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) and \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\), then \(u\equiv 0\). If \(p=\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), then there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) such that \(u\) is radially symmetric and strictly increasing about \(x_0\).
D. If \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) and \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\), then \(u\equiv 0\). If \(p=\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), then there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) such that \(u\) is radially symmetric about \(x_0\).
E. If \(1<p<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) and \(u\in L^{p+1}(\mathbb H^n)\), then \(u\) is strictly positive and radially symmetric about some \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\). If \(p=\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), then there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb H^n\) such that \(u\) is radially symmetric and nondecreasing about \(x_0\).

Let \(K\) be a number field, let \(e\ge 1\) be an integer, and write \(G_K=\mathrm{Gal}(\overline K/K)\), where \(\overline K\) is a fixed algebraic closure of \(K\). For \(\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_e)\in G_K^e\), let \(\overline K(\sigma)\) denote the fixed field of the subgroup of \(G_K\) generated by \(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_e\). Here “almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\)” means all \(\sigma\) outside a subset of Haar measure zero in \(G_K^e\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about every finite extension \(L\) of \(\overline K(\sigma)\) for almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\)?

Options:
A. For almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\), every finite extension \(L/\overline K(\sigma)\) is Kummer-faithful, and this already forces \(L\) to be both torally Kummer-faithful and AVKF.
B. For almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\), every finite extension \(L/\overline K(\sigma)\) is Kummer-faithful.
C. For almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\), every finite extension \(L/\overline K(\sigma)\) is torally Kummer-faithful, while \(\overline K(\sigma)\) itself is AVKF; hence every such \(L\) is Kummer-faithful.
D. For almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\), every algebraic extension \(L/\overline K(\sigma)\) is both torally Kummer-faithful and AVKF, and hence is Kummer-faithful.
E. For almost all \(\sigma\in G_K^e\), every finite extension \(L/\overline K(\sigma)\) is both torally Kummer-faithful and AVKF, and hence is Kummer-faithful.

Let \(\Omega=G\times(-h,0)\) for some horizontal domain \(G\subset\mathbb R^2\), with horizontal variables \((x,y)\), vertical variable \(z\), and boundary parts \(\Gamma_u=G\times\{0\}\), \(\Gamma_b=G\times\{-h\}\), and \(\Gamma_l=\partial G\times(-h,0)\). Let \(u=(v,w)\) solve the three-dimensional primitive equations
\[
\partial_t v+u\cdot \nabla v-\Delta v+\nabla_H \pi=0,\qquad \partial_z\pi=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0
\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
\]
with initial condition
\[
v|_{t=0}=a \quad\text{in }\Omega.
\]
Here \(\nabla_H=(\partial_x,\partial_y)\), \(\operatorname{div}_H\) is the horizontal divergence, and the vertical average is
\[
\bar a(x,y):=\frac1h\int_{-h}^0 a(x,y,z)\,dz.
\]
Assume the initial data satisfy \(a\in H^1(\Omega)\), \(a_z:=\partial_z a\in L^3(\Omega)\), the compatibility condition \(\operatorname{div}_H\bar a=0\), and horizontal periodicity on \(\Gamma_l\). In the mixed boundary-condition case, also assume \(a=0\) on \(\Gamma_b\). Suppose moreover that \(u,\pi\) are periodic on \(\Gamma_l\times(0,T)\) and that either
\[
\partial_z v=0,\quad w=0 \quad\text{on }(\Gamma_u\cup\Gamma_b)\times(0,T),
\]
or
\[
\partial_z v=0,\quad w=0 \quad\text{on }\Gamma_u\times(0,T),
\qquad
v=0,\quad w=0 \quad\text{on }\Gamma_b\times(0,T).
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about \(v\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\) under these assumptions?

Options:
A. It satisfies the bound
\[
\|v(t)\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2
\le B(a)e^{C\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2}
\quad\forall t\in[0,T],
\]
where \(B(a)\) is a polynomial function of \(\|a\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\) and \(\|a_z\|_{L^3(\Omega)}\), and \(C>0\) depends only on \(\Omega\).
B. It satisfies the uniform estimate
\[
\|v(t)\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\int_0^t \|\nabla^2 v(s)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\,ds
\le B(a)e^{C\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2}
\quad\forall t\in[0,T],
\]
where \(B(a)\) is a polynomial function of \(\|a\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\) and \(\|a_z\|_{L^3(\Omega)}\), and \(C>0\) depends only on \(\Omega\); however, this conclusion holds only in the fully Neumann case, while in the mixed boundary-condition case one only gets a time-dependent bound.
C. Under the stated assumptions one can conclude only the estimate
\[
\|v(t)\|_{H^1(\Omega)}
\le B(a,t)e^{C(\sqrt t+1)\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2}
\quad\forall t\in[0,T],
\]
where \(B(a,t)\) is a polynomial function of \(\|a\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\), \(\|a\|_{L^8(\Omega)}\), \(\|a_z\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\), and \(\sqrt t\); in particular, no time-independent bound of the form stated in A is available from these assumptions.
D. It satisfies the a priori estimate
\[
\|v(t)\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\int_0^t \|\nabla^2 v(s)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\,ds
\le B(a)e^{C\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2}
\quad\forall t\in[0,T],
\]
but only after strengthening the hypothesis to \(a_z\in L^4(\Omega)\); under merely \(a_z\in L^3(\Omega)\), one has only the time-dependent proposition-type estimate.
E. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

Let \(T>1\) be a fixed transseries, and let \(\mathbb{R}\wspc{T}\) denote the corresponding field of omega-series in \(T\). Let \(\mathbb{U}^{>\mathbb{R}}\) be the ordered set of inputs \(x\) for which the composition \(f\circ x\) is defined. For a given \(f\in \mathbb{R}\wspc{T}\), consider the map \(x\mapsto f\circ x\) on \(\mathbb{U}^{>\mathbb{R}}\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the monotonicity of this map when \(f'\) is everywhere positive, everywhere negative, or identically zero?

Options:
A. The map \(x\mapsto f\circ x\) is strictly increasing if \(f'>0\), strictly decreasing if \(f'<0\), and only locally constant on \(\mathbb{U}^{>\mathbb{R}}\) if \(f'=0\), with no global constancy conclusion in general.
B. If \(f'>0\), then the map \(x\mapsto f\circ x\) is increasing; if \(f'<0\), then it is decreasing; and if \(f'=0\), then it is constant.
C. The sign of \(f'\) determines the monotonicity of \(x\mapsto f\circ x\) only for those \(f\) that satisfy an additional weak mean-value estimate; for arbitrary omega-series, the derivative sign alone does not suffice.
D. The sign of \(f'\) gives the stated monotonicity conclusion for omega-series obtained from \(T\) by finitely many applications of \(\exp\) and \(\log\), but for genuinely infinite omega-series one can in general conclude only non-strict monotonicity.
E. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

Let $(X,D)$ be a $\mathcal C$-pair. Assume that either (i) $X$ is a compact K\"ahler analytic variety and $(X,D)$ is locally uniformizable, or (ii) $X$ is projective and $(X,D)$ is divisorially log terminal (dlt). Assume in addition that $(X,D)$ is special. Here $q^+(X,D)$ denotes the augmented irregularity of the pair, i.e. the supremum of the irregularities over covers of $X$ compatible with the pair structure. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about $q^+(X,D)$?

Options:
A. One has $q^+(X,D)\leq \dim X-1$.
B. There exists a compatible cover $\gamma:\widehat X\to X$ for which the supremum is attained, i.e. $q(X,D,\gamma)=q^+(X,D)$, and hence $q(X,D,\gamma)\leq \dim X$.
C. If $X$ is projective and $(X,D)$ is dlt, then $q^+(X,D)\leq \dim X$; in the compact K\"ahler locally uniformizable case, one can only conclude that $q^+(X,D)<\infty$.
D. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
E. One has $q^+(X,D)<\infty$.

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold, and let $K\subset M$ be a Liouville domain, meaning a codimension-$0$ submanifold with smooth boundary for which there exists a vector field $X$ on $K$ such that $\mathcal L_X\omega=\omega$; write $\alpha=\iota_X\omega|_{\partial K}$ for the induced contact form on $\partial K$. Assume that $(M,\omega)$ is symplectically aspherical and that the contact manifold $(\partial K,\alpha)$ is index-bounded. Let $SH_M(K)$ denote the relative symplectic cohomology of $K$ in $M$, and let $\hbar(SH_M(K))$ be its barcode entropy. Let $\varphi_\alpha^t$ denote the Reeb flow on $(\partial K,\alpha)$, and let $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1)$ be the topological entropy of its time-$1$ map. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate for $\hbar(SH_M(K))$?

Options:
A. There exists a constant $C=C(\partial K,\alpha)>0$, depending only on the contact manifold $(\partial K,\alpha)$, such that
\[
\hbar(SH_M(K))\le C\,h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1).
\]
B. There exists a constant $C=C(M,K)>0$, depending only on the pair $(M,K)$, such that
\[
\hbar(SH_M(K))\le C\,h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1).
\]
C. The estimate holds with no extra geometric loss, namely
\[
\hbar(SH_M(K))\le h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1).
\]
D. If $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1)=0$, then
\[
\hbar(SH_M(K))=0.
\]
E. There exists a constant $C=C(M)>0$, depending only on the ambient closed symplectic manifold $M$, such that
\[
\hbar(SH_M(K))\le C\,h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1).
\]

Let $p$ be a prime, let $\mathbb F_p$ denote the finite field with $p$ elements, and let $A\subseteq \mathbb F_p$ satisfy $|A|\gg p$ (that is, $|A|$ is at least a positive constant multiple of $p$). Let $(r_1,\ldots,r_k)$ be a generic tuple of integer exponents. For an exponent $r$, write $A^r=\{a^r:a\in A\}$, and define the sumset
\[
A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}=\{a_1^{r_1}+\cdots +a_k^{r_k}:a_i\in A\}.
\]
What is the strongest asymptotic lower bound that can be proved about the size of $A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}$?

Options:
A. \[\big|A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}\big|\ge (1-o(1))\min\big(p^{\frac{k-1}{k}}|A|^{1/k},\,p\big).\]
B. \[\big|A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}\big|\ge (1-o(1))\min\big(k\,p^{\frac{k-1}{k}}|A|^{1/k},\,p\big)\quad\text{for every tuple }(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\text{ of integer exponents}.\]
C. \[\big|A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}\big|\ge (1-o(1))\,k\,p^{\frac{k-1}{k}}|A|^{1/k}.\]
D. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
E. \[\big|A^{r_1}+\cdots +A^{r_k}\big|\ge (1-o(1))\,k\,\min\big(p^{\frac{k-1}{k}}|A|^{1/k},\,p\big).\]

Let $R$ be a ring, let $\mathsf D(R)$ denote the derived category of $R$-modules, and write $\mathsf{pgdim}(-)$ for projective generating dimension. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the inequality between $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R))$ and $\mathsf{pgdim}(R)$ for every ring $R$?

Options:
A. For every ring $R$ with $\mathsf{pgdim}(R)\geq 2$, one has $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R))\geq 2$.
B. For every ring $R$, one has $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R)) \leq \mathsf{pgdim}(R)$.
C. For every ring $R$, one has $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R)) \geq \mathsf{pgdim}(R)$.
D. For every ring $R$ with $\mathsf{pgdim}(R)\geq 2$, one has $1\leq \mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R)) \leq \mathsf{pgdim}(R)-1$.
E. For every ring $R$ with $\mathsf{pgdim}(R)\geq 2$, one has $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R)) \leq \mathsf{pgdim}(R)-1$.

A positive integer is called square-full if every prime dividing it divides it to exponent at least 2. For a real parameter $B\ge 1$, let $n(B)$ denote the number of triples $(u,v,w)$ of positive integers, each square-full, satisfying $u+v=w$ and $w\le B$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate for $n(B)$?

Options:
A. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
B. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ one has
\[
n(B)\ll_{\varepsilon} B^{1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
C. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ one has
\[
n(B)\ll_{\varepsilon} B^{3/5-1/500+\varepsilon}.
\]
D. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ one has
\[
n(B)\ll B^{3/5-3/1555+\varepsilon},
\]
with an implied constant absolute (in particular, independent of $\varepsilon$).
E. There exists a constant $\delta>0$ such that
\[
n(B)\ll B^{3/5-\delta}.
\]

Let \(\Omega_{\lambda}\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) be the ambient open set depending on \(\lambda\). Let \(n\ge 4\) and define
\[
\bar\lambda(n)=\frac12\frac{n-3}{\sqrt{n-2}}.
\]
Assume \(0<\lambda\le \bar\lambda(n)\), and let
\[
E=\{(x,t)\in \mathbb R^{n+1}:x_1>0\}.
\]
Write \(P(A;U)\) for the relative perimeter of a set \(A\) in a region \(U\). Say that \(F\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) has locally finite perimeter if \(P(F;U)<\infty\) for every \(U\subset\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\). Let \(B_R=B_R(0,0)\) denote the Euclidean ball of radius \(R\), and let \(E\Delta F\) denote symmetric difference. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate satisfied by every locally finite perimeter set \(F\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) such that \(E\Delta F\subset\subset B_R\) for some \(R>0\)?

Options:
A. \[
P(E;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)\le P(F;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)+\mathcal H^n\big((E\Delta F)\cap \partial\Omega_{\lambda}\big).
\]
for every locally finite perimeter set \(F\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) with \(E\Delta F\subset\subset B_R\) for some \(R>0\).
B. \[
P(E;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)+\mathcal H^n\big((E\Delta F)\cap \partial\Omega_{\lambda}\big)\le P(F;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R).
\]
C. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.
D. \[
P(E;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)\le P(F;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)
\]
for every locally finite perimeter set \(F\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) such that \(E\Delta F\subset\subset B_R\), provided \(0<\lambda<\bar\lambda(n)\).
E. \[
P(E;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)\le P(F;\Omega_{\lambda}\cap B_R)
\]
for every locally finite perimeter set \(F\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}\) with \(E\Delta F\subset\subset B_R\) for some \(R>0\), for every \(\lambda>0\).

Let \(u=u(t,x)\) solve the Ohta--Kawasaki equation on \((0,\infty)\times(0,L)\) with \(L=2\pi\),
\[
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}=-\dfrac{1}{\gamma^2}\dfrac{\partial^4 u}{\partial x^4}-\dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x^2}(u-u^3)-\sigma(u-m), & (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times(0,L), \\
\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}(t,0)=\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}(t,L)=\dfrac{\partial^3 u}{\partial x^3}(t,0)=\dfrac{\partial^3 u}{\partial x^3}(t,L)=0, & t\ge 0, \\
 u(0,x)=u_{\mathrm{in}}(x), & x\in[0,L],
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\gamma=\sqrt{8}\), \(\sigma=1/5\), \(m=1/10\), and
\[
 u_{\mathrm{in}}(x)=m+\frac{2}{10}\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi x}{L}\right)+\frac{2}{10}\cos\!\left(\frac{4\pi x}{L}\right).
\]
Let \(\bar u(t,x)\) be the specified approximate solution, described in terms of Chebyshev\(\times\)Fourier coefficients, given on \([0,30]\times[0,L]\) and extended to all \(t\ge 30\) by \(\bar u(t,x)=\bar u(30,x)\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the error between the exact solution \(u\) and this approximate solution \(\bar u\)?

Options:
A. \[\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\sup_{x\in[0,L]}\big|u(t,x)-\bar u(t,x)\big|\le 4\times 10^{-8}.\]
B. \[\sup_{x\in[0,L]}\big|u(30,x)-\bar u(30,x)\big|\le 9\times 10^{-7}.\]
C. \[\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\sup_{x\in[0,L]}\big|u(t,x)-\bar u(30,x)\big|\le 9\times 10^{-7}.\]
D. \[\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\left\|u(t,\cdot)-\bar u(t,\cdot)\right\|_{L^2(0,L)}\le 9\times 10^{-7}.\]
E. One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

Let \(q(G)\) denote the largest eigenvalue of the signless Laplacian of a graph \(G\). Suppose \(G\) is a connected outerplanar graph of order \(n\) (that is, with \(n\) vertices) that is \(C_\ell\)-free, where \(\ell\ge 3\). Let \(P_t\) be the path on \(t\) vertices, let \(\alpha P_{\ell-2}\) mean the disjoint union of \(\alpha\) copies of \(P_{\ell-2}\), let \(\cup\) denote disjoint union, and let \(\vee\) denote graph join. Define
\[
\alpha=\left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{\ell-2}\right\rfloor,\qquad r=n-1-\alpha(\ell-2),
\]
and, if \(r=0\), interpret \(P_r=P_0\) as the empty graph. Which quantitative estimate holds for \(q(G)\)?

Options:
A. \(q(G)\le q\bigl(K_1\vee (\alpha P_{\ell-2}\cup P_r)\bigr)\), with equality if and only if \(G\) has a dominating vertex \(v\) such that the components of \(G-v\) have orders \(\ell-2,\ldots,\ell-2,r\).
